Make the clock visible.

CH8-01 · Separate signal information, execution and the earned holding interval.

A backtest reconstructs a rule’s hypothetical actions from supplied data. Before calculation, freeze this rule: after close t, average the latest three closes including t. If close t is strictly above that mean, target weight 1; otherwise target 0. Execute at open t+1 and earn the open t+1→open t+2 return. Do not tune the three-close window.

Signal after close t → execute open t+1 → mark open t+2

Worked: Jan 2–4 closes are 100,101,102, mean101. Jan4 close102>101 implies target1. It first buys at Jan5 open103, then marks at Jan6 open100. Its first gross holding return is 100/103−1=−2.9126%. Using the earlier Jan4 close as the execution price would pretend to trade at a price already used to calculate the decision.

Warm-up rows provide three closes and earn no strategy return here. The final close is not used to make an unexecutable signal. Each holding interval ends at the next open; final liquidation is separately charged at the last eligible open. Prices are original positive synthetic values, not split-adjusted market data. They have no distributions or corporate actions to adjust.

Translate the rule without hindsight.

CH8-02 · Reconstruct target weights and detect future-data contamination.

A target weight of 1 means fully invested; 0 means cash. This example permits no leverage or short positions. Cash earns zero, so a cash interval has zero gross return before any transaction costs. The strict “above” condition sends a tie to cash.

Worked second signal: Jan3–5 closes101,102,101 have mean101.3333. Jan5 close101 is below that mean: target0 at Jan6 open100. The prior position1 was held Jan5→Jan6. At Jan6 open it sells to cash and incurs exit costs; it does not retroactively avoid the loss it already earned.

Predict: if the final future close changes, can the first position change? It must not. Each target uses only the three closes ending on its own signal date. A future perturbation test detects many timing mistakes, although passing it does not prove the entire implementation correct. Our tests also check hand arithmetic, matched benchmarks and costs.

All supplied runs, including disappointing ones, belong in a trial log. Viewing the transfer data in this course counts as exposure. A label “evaluation” alone is not proof of independent validation. Chapter9 prepares an honest plan and disclosure; Chapter10 reports evidence within those limits.

Pay for entry and exit.

CH8-03 · Apply turnover costs before the period return and include final liquidation.

One basis point (bp) is 0.01%; 10 bps is .10%=.001 as a decimal. For target w and previous target wprev, turnover is |w−wprev|. The fee is cost rate c times this fraction of current wealth. Charge the fee first, then earn the holding return.

V after interval = V before × (1−c|w−wprev|) × (1+w r)
Final liquidation = V × (1−c wlast)

Worked: £1000, previous0,target1,10bps,+10% return →1000×.999×1.1=£1098.90. Final exit costs another £1.0989, leaving £1097.8011. A 1→0 transition also has turnover1. No change in a 0/1 target means zero turnover. This simplified discrete all-in/cash rule avoids intermediate-weight drift.

For the supplied Jan example the first step is £1000×.999×100/103=£969.9029. The following exit at10bps reduces that cash balance too. If prices are flat but the benchmark buys and later sells, its final wealth is £1000×.999²=£998.001. A cost-free result is not a net result.

No additional bid–ask spread, market impact, slippage, taxes, default, borrow fees or cash interest is modelled. This fee is a teaching proxy, not a complete execution model. Increasing a nonnegative fee with an unchanged fixed position path cannot improve ending wealth here. Do not search fees or windows for the nicest return.

Match the comparison window.

CH8-04 · Evaluate the rule and buy-and-hold over identical eligible opens with consistent costs.

The benchmark starts with the same £1000, buys at the strategy’s first eligible execution open, holds through the same final eligible open and sells there. It pays the same per-notional fee on entry and final exit. Both series omit warm-up performance and use zero-interest cash, no leverage and the same prices.

On the development table, both eligible windows are Jan5 open£103→Jan17 open£108. Cost-free benchmark growth is108/103−1=4.8544%. At10bps its final wealth is1000×.999×108/103×.999=£1046.4477. The strategy uses different weights inside these dates, so it can have different growth and risk. Ending wealth alone is not a complete risk comparison.

Predict: would a benchmark starting at Jan2 open£100 be comparable? No: it includes days excluded from the strategy. A strategy can appear better or worse simply because dates differ. Use the table’s explicit signal, entry and exit dates to inspect alignment.

Development dates are Jan2–17,2025. A separate, already-visible transfer table spans Feb3–12,2025, with eligible opens Feb6–12. These tiny authored segments are teaching cases, not market evidence or a secure holdout. This chapter does not establish profitability, robustness, out-of-sample validation or an investable recommendation.

Rubric:explicit model/timing;arithmetic including all cash flows;honest limits;response to feedback. Prose is self-reviewed,not automatically graded.
